feuchte.titel: Wet wood costs you half the heat
feuchte.einleitung: A kilogram of wood always holds the same energy. What decides how much of it reaches the room is the water inside: it has to evaporate first, and that evaporation consumes heat which then warms nobody.
feuchte.bildAlt: Logs burning in a wood stove
feuchte.grenzwert: France Bois Bûche label threshold (class H1)

frisch.text: Straight out of the forest. It smokes, sooties up the glass — and simply must not be burned in that state.

luft.text: Under cover, ventilated, stacked away from the wall. After two summers, that is the realistic best case.

kammer.text: 72 hours at 75 °C. We measure every batch and enclose the record with the delivery.

feuchte.fussnote: The France Bois Bûche label and standard NF EN ISO 17225-5 class wood at or below 20 % moisture content as H1. Air-dried wood reaches that figure after roughly two summers; kiln-dried wood leaves production that way. A moisture meter costs under €20 and settles any argument — measure on a freshly split log, never on the outer face.

holzarten.einleitung: The figures are for wood at 20 % moisture content, in kilowatt-hours per stacked cubic metre. Spruce is in the table even though we only sell it as kindling: its place is at the start of a fire, not in the sustained load.
holzarten.fussnote: Source: calorific value tables from the French chambers of agriculture, commercially rounded. 1 stacked cubic metre equals roughly 1.4 loose cubic metres.

faq.titel: What buyers want to know beforehand
faq.einleitung: If your question is not here, give us a call. Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to 1pm, the person who picks up has delivered the wood themselves.

srm.frage: What is the difference between a loose cubic metre, a stacked cubic metre and a solid cubic metre?
srm.antwort: A loose cubic metre is a cubic metre of wood tipped in loose, just as it falls out of the bin. Neatly stacked, the same quantity comes to roughly 0.7 stacked cubic metres. Take out all the air between the logs and about 0.4 solid cubic metres of actual wood remains. We sell by the loose cubic metre, because that is the quantity that actually arrives at your place.

trocken.frage: How do I know the wood is really dry?
trocken.antwort: By the sound and the cracks: dry logs ring bright when you knock two together, and show star-shaped cracks on the end grain. Only measuring is certain. Push the moisture meter into a freshly split log, not into the outer face — on the outside, even wet wood reads dry. Our measurement record comes with every delivery.

lagern.frage: How do I store the wood after delivery?
lagern.antwort: Kiln-dried wood no longer needs to dry, but it must not get wet again. Under cover, away from the wall and not directly on the ground — a pallet underneath is enough. In a closed cellar without ventilation, wood draws moisture from the air and is back above 20 % within a year.

restaurant.frage: Do you also deliver to restaurants and bakeries?
restaurant.antwort: Yes. For wood-fired ovens and grill restaurants we supply beech in 25 and 33 cm at under 15 % moisture content, on weekly call-off if wanted. From three pallets a month a separate tiered price applies. Write to us via the contact form and we'll reply the same working day.

livraison.frage: How much does delivery cost, and how long does it take?
livraison.antwort: Standard delivery is free, with no minimum order, within 3 to 5 working days. Express delivery costs €60 and arrives within 24 to 48 hours. We deliver anywhere in France and to selected towns in Belgium: in France on our own trailer, elsewhere on a pallet by freight carrier. Either way, you are told before we come.

abladen.frage: Where exactly is the wood left?
abladen.antwort: Kerbside unloading is included in the price. We carry pallet trucks, so pallets can be taken through to your garage or storage bay. Tell us about a narrow entrance, a low gate or an enclosed courtyard when you order and we will bring the right vehicle.
